keptItems.title: Trump’s Attacks on the Media Are Self-Defeating
keptItems.summaryEvidence: Donald Trump is presiding over a failing presidency and lashing out at the news media—most recently by banning CNN, Politico , and MS NOW from the White House. There might seem to be a connection between these two things, but the causal link is not that Trump is punishing the press because he is failing ; rather, it’s the opposite. His inability to govern is in part a consequence of his hatred for the news media. Trump has been bullying and manipulating the news media since before he entered politics. And though it may be tempting to believe that his efforts to strangle independent reporting result from his current political travails, he has been pursuing that project throughout his current term. Trump attempted to ban the Associated Press from the White House during his first days in office, when his popularity was at its short-lived apogee. Trump’s most dangerous moves against the media came in the wake of Charlie Kirk’s assassination, when some conservatives perceived that the tragedy handed them a window to discredit their critics. In fair weather and foul, Trump simply cannot tolerate critical news coverage. His belief that the mainstream news media is profoundly biased against him and his party is an article of faith on the political right, although he has pushed much further in response to that belief than any of his predecessors ever dared. keptItems.title: Trump’s Monumental Obsession
keptItems.summaryEvidence: Donald Trump is facing multiple challenges. The United States is losing to one of its worst enemies in a war that has left the American economy mired in the sludge of growing inflation and rising energy prices. His popularity is now hovering around second-term George W. Bush levels, and may even be headed for end-stage Richard Nixon numbers. His party faces the prospect of a crushing defeat in midterm elections that are only six weeks away. (In some places, early voting has already begun.) The country and the 47th president’s administration are in trouble on every front. Despite all of this military, economic, and political chaos, Trump has stayed true to a handful of projects: renaming the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, demolishing the East Wing of the White House and replacing it with a ballroom that even the French kings might have thought over the top, and building a triumphal arch in front of the bridge to Arlington Cemetery whose design looks like it was found in the bottom of Albert Speer’s desk drawer. The president is very concerned about these undertakings. He is, as they say in Washington, laser-focused on them. Ordinary folks might say “obsessed,” because at times he seems unable to talk about anything else, even when asked about matters of national importance, including America’s slow-motion defeat in the Middle East.
